method: Hand-written single-best-answer MCQs grounded only in the accepted open full text.

topic.coverageNote: Trochanteric bursitis is handled as part of GTPS, which is the diagnosis the source says should replace isolated-bursitis labelling.

mcqs.question: How does this review define the scope of greater trochanteric pain syndrome?

options.A: Peritrochanteric disorders including trochanteric bursitis, abductor tendon pathology, and external snapping hip
options.B: Isolated septic arthritis of the hip
options.C: Osteoarthritis of the knee referred to the hip
options.D: Only fracture of the greater trochanter

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Peritrochanteric disorders including trochanteric bursitis, abductor tendon pathology, and external snapping hip
mcqs.explanation: GTPS describes disorders of the peritrochanteric space, including trochanteric bursitis, abductor tendon pathology, and external coxa saltans.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Greater trochanteric pain syndrome (GTPS) is a general term used to describe disorders of the peritrochanteric space, including trochanteric bursitis, abductor tendon pathology, and external coxa saltans.

mcqs.question: What have radiographic and histologic studies shown about isolated trochanteric bursitis?

options.A: The bursae are rarely affected in isolation; distention is usually associated with tendon pathology
options.B: Every case of lateral hip pain is isolated bursitis
options.E: Histology shows infection in most bursae

mcqs.correctAnswerText: The bursae are rarely affected in isolation; distention is usually associated with tendon pathology
mcqs.explanation: The trochanteric bursae are rarely affected in isolation. Bursal distention is most commonly associated with tendon pathology.

sourceRefs.excerpt: the trochanteric bursae are rarely affected in isolation

mcqs.question: In the surgical series summarized here, how common were gluteus medius tendinopathy and bursitis with tendinopathy?

options.A: Gluteus medius tendinopathy in 62.5%, and trochanteric bursitis with tendinopathy in 8.3%

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Gluteus medius tendinopathy in 62.5%, and trochanteric bursitis with tendinopathy in 8.3%
mcqs.explanation: The review reports gluteus medius tendinopathy in 62.5% and trochanteric bursitis with concomitant tendinopathy in 8.3% of that surgical series.

sourceRefs.excerpt: 62.5% had gluteus medius tendinopathy, and 8.3% had trochanteric bursitis with concomitant tendinopathy

mcqs.question: Which conservative treatments does the review say many patients have already failed?

options.A: Physical therapy, NSAIDs, and corticosteroid injections
options.E: The review says conservative care is never used

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Physical therapy, NSAIDs, and corticosteroid injections
mcqs.explanation: Many patients demonstrate symptoms refractory to physical therapy, NSAIDs, and corticosteroid injections.

sourceRefs.excerpt: many demonstrate symptoms refractory to physical therapy, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), and corticosteroid injections

mcqs.question: In the 120-patient comparison, what recovery difference did adding a corticosteroid injection make at 3 months?

options.A: 55% strongly or fully recovered with the injection versus 34% with analgesics and physical therapy alone
options.B: 34% recovered with the injection versus 55% without it
options.E: The injection group had more pain and no recovery difference

mcqs.correctAnswerText: 55% strongly or fully recovered with the injection versus 34% with analgesics and physical therapy alone
mcqs.explanation: At 3 months, 55% of the corticosteroid-injection group had strongly or fully recovered, compared with 34% of the analgesics and physical therapy group, and the injection group reported greater pain improvement.

sourceRefs.excerpt: 55% of the CSI group had strongly or fully recovered at 3 months compared with 34% of the solely analgesics and physical therapy group
